Consider the following numbers and tick the box next to every one that is irrational.

generalfeedback.text:
{@n1@} and {@n2@} are rational: one is a whole number, the other a ratio of two integers.

\( \sqrt{ {@n3_base@}^2 } = {@n3@} \) looks irrational because of the square root symbol, but \( {@n3_base@}^2 \) is a perfect square, so it simplifies to a whole number - it is rational.

\( \sqrt{ {@n4_base@} } \) and \( \sqrt{ {@n5_base@} } \) are irrational, because {@n4_base@} and {@n5_base@} are not perfect squares, so their square roots cannot be simplified to integers or fractions.

\( \pi \) is irrational - it is a well-known non-repeating, non-terminating decimal.

Always simplify a number fully before deciding whether it is rational or irrational.
